I measured both in the layout of 6.4 itself (X1 = X10 = 0, shared seed words, X12 < 2^8, X13 < 2^16, all 65,536 members in batch order) on CPU: 24 runs of 2^30 trials. Share of trials satisfying rule A times 64: 0.999565 to 1.000452, all runs 1.000029, chi-square 18.7 on 24. The batch share is below 1-(63/64)^7 = 0.104379 by about 20 standard deviations, so neighbouring members are positively correlated in rule A; that is harmless for the budget. findings.where: proof.md lines 1227-1231 and 1924-1929; claim.json H1 limitations ("rests on one SAT solver's uncertified answers"); tools\rule_a_sat.py
findings.what: The 247 "unsatisfiable" answers hold up, and the stated limitation can be reduced. With my own CNF encoder in a different formulation (b and d output differences forced instead of psi), cadical, kissat and cryptominisat5 each give UNSAT for the same 247 outcomes and SAT for the same 40; all 40 models are violating solutions in plain arithmetic. The count rebuilt from my answers is 29,965,882.5 with 12,039.8 dropped; the four heaviest betas keep their full parts (16, 10, 10 and 12 outcomes, all UNSAT). For all 247, cadical with its internal DRAT and LRAT checkers on (--check --checkproof=3) returns UNSAT with no checker abort. A forward RUP checker written for this review accepts every lemma of 247 plain-CDCL proofs (897,039 lemmas, none rejected) and refutes all 247 formulas; as a control it never refutes the satisfiable formula with the same proof. Files: review\math_sat.py, math_proof.py, math_proof.txt.
findings.fix: Optional: add a second solver and a proof check to tools\rule_a_sat.py (cadical --check --checkproof=3, or the RUP checker in review\math_proof.py), keep the result in evidence\, and replace "one solver in one run; no proof certificate was kept or checked" by what was done. As written the text is true and conservative.

findings.where: proof.md lines 1081-1084 and 1239-1249 (the three betas c81cd8b3, f81c2873, f81c28b3); submission-note-r2.md near line 220; the same sentence in research\pkg4
findings.what: The caveat on the three betas can be closed. I encoded the whole seven-word system (E1 and E3 on both messages, R = 0 as four digest-word equations, Y4 in the class, beta fixed, no tau or eps prescribed). cadical and kissat both find no solution for these three betas, so their part is exactly zero. Over all 4,272 betas of the list, cadical finds the system satisfiable for exactly the 39 betas with a part and unsatisfiable for the other 4,233. For each of the 39, cadical and kissat find no solution whose outcome is outside the calculator's 287, and a rule-A-violating solution exists for exactly the 14 betas of the dropped table (my 14 models all lie in dropped outcomes). These are solver answers without certificates. Files: review\math_seven.py, math_seven_any_cadical.txt, math_seven_other_*.txt, math_seven_violate_*.txt.
